headline: Take-Two rockets +6% on monster GTA VI pre-orders, gold hits record highs, and Netanyahu rejects Trump's Gaza plan — a busy Monday to close the week.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: GTA VI pre-orders have reportedly hit eye-watering levels, sending the stock surging last night. Take-Two's earnings call also confirmed the company is laser-focused on the single-player game first, not rushing into GTA Online. The market loves the pre-order momentum — this is the core thesis playing out in real time.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS bounced +3% at today's close, likely riding a broader risk-on mood on the ASX. The lithium market remains challenging — a separate report on GL1 highlighted ongoing headwinds for developers — but Pilbara as a producer is better placed than most. Still well underwater on your cost base, though.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI closed up +2.4% today, likely benefiting from positive AI sentiment flowing through from last night's strong NASDAQ session (+1.3%). The ETF holds a basket of global AI stocks, so a tech rally in the US tends to lift it the next day on the ASX.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE edged up +0.6% today. Emerging markets got a mild boost from a slightly stronger Aussie dollar (AUD/USD up to 0.707) and the positive global risk tone from last night's US session.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS crept up +0.26% today — the ASX-listed version of the broad US market tracked last night's S&P 500 gains (+0.62%). Steady as she goes.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG nudged up a touch today. As a diversified multi-asset fund it moves slowly — the mild gain reflects the generally positive global backdrop last night.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft was essentially flat last night at just under $500, hovering just below the psychologically important $500 mark. Erste Group Bank has upgraded its earnings forecasts for MSFT, and the Copilot AI product is driving new business. No drama here.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: GOOG dipped -0.88% last night in what looks like a mild profit-take after recent strength. The fundamental story remains very strong — Google Cloud just posted 82% year-over-year revenue growth, and analysts reckon next quarter could be even better. The dip is noise, not a signal.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA VI pre-orders are massive — hold and enjoy the ride
watch_today.detail: Take-Two surged +6% last night on reports that GTA VI pre-orders have hit 'eye-watering' levels. The earnings call confirmed single-player is the focus before any GTA Online push. This is the exact long-term thesis you bought into. No reason to sell — sit tight and let this play out over the next 12+ months as the game approaches launch.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Bouncing but still deeply underwater — hold and be patient
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals had a decent +3% day today but you're still down ~30% on your position (-$45 AUD). Lithium market headwinds are real and the outlook remains uncertain. However, Pilbara is a quality producer with real assets. For a long-term holder, this isn't the time to crystallise a loss — the thesis depends on a lithium demand recovery over years, not months.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX: Good day, but still in the red — hold through AI cycle
watch_today.detail: GXAI bounced +2.4% today following the strong NASDAQ session last night. You're still down 13% on the position (-$39 AUD). The AI investment cycle is accelerating globally — OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google are all heading to a White House AI safety summit, and South Australia just launched a royal commission into AI, showing government attention is growing. Long-term, the sector tailwind is strong. Hold.

watch_today.title: RBA rate decision — watch this week for mortgage and market impact
watch_today.detail: The RBA is widely expected to cut rates this week, but analysts are warning the relief could be short-lived. Some economists and the AFR are arguing the RBA should actually hold or even hike, and markets are pricing in a risk of one more rate rise this year. A cut would be positive for growth assets like your ETFs; a surprise hold could spook the ASX. Keep an eye on the announcement and the language the board uses.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Dip looks like noise — long-term story is intact
watch_today.detail: GOOG slipped -0.88% last night but Google Cloud just reported 82% year-over-year revenue growth and analysts expect the next quarter to be even stronger. The stock is up nearly 15% on your cost base. Nothing has changed with the long-term investment case — this is just a small pullback in a strong trend.

watch_today.title: Gold surging to record highs — positive backdrop for your ETFs
watch_today.detail: Gold hit $4,413 USD per ounce last night, up 1.67% — a record high. This usually signals investors are nervous about geopolitical risk (Gaza, Iran/Hormuz Strait tensions) and seeking safe havens. Your diversified ETFs (VDHG, VTS) have some exposure to this risk-off mood, but the broader US market stayed positive last night, which is reassuring.

world.summary: The Middle East is dominating global headlines — Netanyahu has rejected Trump's Gaza ceasefire plan, Iran is playing hardball over the Strait of Hormuz, and Trump is reportedly floating the idea of walking away from Iran nuclear talks entirely. Gold is hitting record highs as investors price in the uncertainty.

stories.title: Netanyahu rejects Trump-backed Gaza ceasefire and disarmament plan
stories.why_it_matters: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has publicly rejected a new US-backed Gaza peace plan that would have seen Hamas disarm and Israeli forces withdraw from the territory. This is a significant split — Trump's own advisers are calling the plan 'the only way forward,' but Netanyahu is refusing. The war in Gaza is now in direct conflict with Trump's diplomatic agenda, which raises the risk of a prolonged stalemate. For everyday Australians, this keeps geopolitical uncertainty elevated, which is part of why gold is surging to record highs.

stories.title: Trump reportedly willing to walk away from Iran war without a nuclear deal
stories.why_it_matters: Reports are emerging that Donald Trump may be prepared to end US military involvement in the Iran conflict without securing a full nuclear deal — essentially declaring a win and leaving. This would be a massive shift in US Middle East policy. If true, it could reduce the risk of a wider regional war, but it also leaves Iran's nuclear program unresolved. Markets and oil traders are watching closely, as any escalation around Iran directly threatens the Strait of Hormuz shipping lane.

stories.title: Iran says a deal on the Strait of Hormuz is close — but not enough to reopen it yet
stories.why_it_matters: Iran has acknowledged that negotiations over reopening the Strait of Hormuz — the narrow waterway through which about 20% of the world's oil flows — are progressing, but says a deal isn't close enough to actually open it yet. A blocked Strait of Hormuz would send global oil prices sharply higher, which feeds through to higher petrol prices and inflation everywhere. This is one to keep watching — oil is holding relatively steady at $78/barrel for now, suggesting markets aren't fully pricing in a crisis yet.

stories.title: Gold hits record high above $4,413 USD per ounce
stories.why_it_matters: Gold surged 1.67% last night to above $4,413 USD per ounce — a fresh record. Gold typically spikes when investors are worried about global instability and want somewhere safe to park their money. The combination of the Gaza deadlock, Iran tensions, and uncertainty about Trump's foreign policy is driving this. For Australian investors, a higher gold price generally benefits ASX-listed gold miners and can be a drag on growth assets if fear really takes hold, though last night's US equity markets stayed positive.

stories.title: AUD/USD rises to 0.707 as US dollar softens
stories.why_it_matters: The Australian dollar climbed to 70.7 US cents last night, up about 0.5%. This typically happens when traders think the US Federal Reserve (the American central bank) will be less aggressive with interest rates, making the US dollar less attractive. A stronger AUD is good news for Australians travelling or buying US goods, but it slightly reduces the AUD value of your US-denominated holdings like GOOG, MSFT, and TTWO — every US dollar of profit is worth a few cents less when converted back.

markets.summary: Last night's US session was broadly positive — the NASDAQ jumped 1.3% and the S&P 500 gained 0.6%, driven by tech strength. The ASX had a quieter Monday, slipping slightly (-0.33%). Gold is at record highs, oil is flat, and the AUD nudged higher against the US dollar.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Mild pullback today after recent strength. Nothing dramatic.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session — solid gains led by tech.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Last night — strong tech rally, TTWO a big contributor.

indicators.name: Gold (WTI)
indicators.note: Record high — geopolitical fear driving safe-haven demand.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Effectively flat — Hormuz tensions not fully priced in yet.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar strengthening — slightly reduces AUD value of US holdings.

politics.summary: The RBA rate decision is the big domestic story this week, with economists divided on whether a cut is actually the right move. Meanwhile, the Albanese government is trying to get gambling reforms over the line by offering the Coalition concessions, and Labor's budget is under fire from the Opposition.

stories.title: RBA expected to cut rates this week — but experts warn 'buckle up' for more pain ahead
stories.why_it_matters: Markets are widely expecting the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) to cut interest rates at its meeting this week, which would be a relief for mortgage holders. However, multiple economists are warning the cut may be short-lived — some, including the AFR's editorial line, are arguing the RBA should hold or even raise rates to fight lingering inflation. Financial Newswire reports markets are still pricing in the risk of one more rate hike before year's end. If you have a mortgage, a cut this week is welcome but don't assume rates are heading back to near-zero anytime soon.

stories.title: Albanese offers Coalition concessions to pass gambling reforms
stories.why_it_matters: Prime Minister Albanese has signalled he's prepared to offer amendments to his gambling advertising reform bill in order to get it through parliament with Coalition support. A Guardian inquiry also heard shocking evidence that alcohol and cocaine were being offered to gamblers by some operators. The reforms aim to restrict gambling advertising, particularly around live sports. For everyday Australians, this would mean significantly fewer betting ads during footy and cricket — the key question now is whether Labor's concessions go too far and water down the reforms.

stories.title: Shadow Treasurer slams Labor's budget as economic 'havoc'
stories.why_it_matters: The Coalition's Shadow Treasurer has come out swinging against the Albanese government's latest budget, claiming it will create economic chaos. This is standard political point-scoring ahead of the next election cycle, but the underlying tension — how to balance spending on cost-of-living relief while keeping inflation under control — is a real challenge. With the RBA watching government spending closely as it decides on interest rates, the budget debate has direct implications for every Australian's mortgage.

ai.summary: AI governance is the dominant theme today — the White House is pulling the big AI labs into a safety meeting, South Australia is launching a royal commission into AI, and there's a growing debate about whether regulators are learning the wrong lessons from social media. Meanwhile, Alphabet's AI cloud investments are paying off big time.

stories.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google called to White House AI safety meeting
stories.why_it_matters: The three biggest AI companies in the world — OpenAI (ChatGPT), Anthropic (Claude), and Google (Gemini) — have been summoned to a White House meeting on AI safety. This signals the US government is getting serious about oversight of powerful AI systems. For your GOOG and GXAI holdings, this is a double-edged sword: more regulation could slow development, but it also legitimises the industry and may lock in the dominant players' advantages.

stories.title: South Australia launches royal commission into AI
stories.why_it_matters: The South Australian government has announced a royal commission — one of the most powerful investigative tools available to Australian governments — into artificial intelligence. This makes SA the first Australian state to take such a formal, high-level look at AI's impact on jobs, services, and society. The outcomes could shape how AI is regulated and used across Australia. For your GXAI.AX holding, increased government scrutiny is something to be aware of, though Australian regulation alone is unlikely to derail the global AI investment thesis.

stories.title: Alphabet's Google Cloud posts 82% revenue growth — and the next quarter could be better
stories.why_it_matters: Google's cloud computing arm just posted 82% year-over-year revenue growth — meaning it's nearly doubled its cloud revenue compared to this time last year. Analysts are arguing this growth rate actually justifies Google's massive capital spending (data centres, chips, AI infrastructure) that some investors had been worried about. For your GOOG holding, this is a very strong signal that the AI investment is paying off, and last night's small dip looks even more like a non-event against this backdrop.

stories.title: AI regulation debate: are we repeating social media's mistakes?
stories.why_it_matters: A new analysis argues that governments are about to make the same mistakes with AI regulation that they made with social media — acting too slowly, letting companies self-regulate for too long, and then scrambling to catch up after harms have already spread. The piece suggests AI needs proactive, structural rules now rather than reactive band-aids later. This is a useful framing for understanding why the White House AI summit and South Australia's royal commission are happening at the same time — there's a growing political consensus that the window for getting ahead of AI risks is closing fast.

sport.summary: NRL Round 23 is done and dusted — the Knights are into the finals after a Raiders brain explosion, Cronulla have injury and suspension news heading into Round 24, and the AFL trade period is heating up with Zak Butters attracting a club-record offer. PNG Chiefs are also making big NRL signings.

stories.title: Knights clinch finals spot as Raiders suffer stunning brain explosion
stories.why_it_matters: The Newcastle Knights locked in a finals berth after Canberra Raiders suffered what Fox Sports called a 'horror' brain explosion late in the game. It caps a terrible year for the Raiders, who are now in danger of missing the top eight. The Knights will face Gold Coast Titans in Round 24 on Sunday at McDonald Jones Stadium.

stories.title: Sharks star faces ban, plus fresh injury blow ahead of Round 24
stories.why_it_matters: A Cronulla Sharks player is set to learn his fate following a brutal high shot during the Sharks' upset loss in Round 23. On top of the suspension news, Cronulla are also dealing with a fresh injury that Fox Sports says will 'hurt' the club heading into their Round 24 clash against the Raiders at Ocean Protect Stadium on Saturday.

stories.title: PNG Chiefs land Brian To'o in major NRL coup ahead of 2027 season
stories.why_it_matters: The incoming PNG Chiefs — the NRL's 18th franchise — have signed Samoan and Penrith Panthers star Brian To'o in a major coup. To'o is one of the best wingers in the competition, and his signing gives the Chiefs instant credibility and star power as they prepare for their first NRL season. The Chiefs tracker shows a squad rapidly taking shape.

stories.title: AFL: Collingwood lock in top-10 spot, Zak Butters attracts club-record offer
stories.why_it_matters: Collingwood secured a top-10 AFL finish with a win over West Coast Eagles, putting themselves in finals contention heading into the back half of the season. Separately, Port Adelaide midfielder Zak Butters is attracting a club-record financial offer from a big Victorian club — the trade period is heating up well ahead of October.
